definition: A missing capability or functionality in a software product that competitors or alternatives offer.
extendedDefinition: A feature gap is the difference between what a software product offers and what a buyer's workflow actually requires, usually identified when a competitor has a capability the candidate lacks. Understanding gaps early is critical: teams that discover them after deployment face costly workarounds, shadow spreadsheets, or custom development. A structured gap analysis begins with a prioritized feature list built from real users, then maps each requirement against vendor offerings and integration points. Not all gaps are equal: some can be closed with configuration, integrations, or roadmap promises, while others indicate a true mismatch. Buyers should be explicit about which gaps are deal-breakers and which are acceptable trade-offs, then validate high-priority gaps during the trial. Recording gaps also strengthens negotiation, since vendors often respond to concrete, ranked requirements with pricing or roadmap commitments.
